Starting artifacts / scaffolds / reuse

Templates give the work a useful first shape.

A reusable starting artifact or scaffold that can be copied, instantiated, or adapted to accelerate a specific kind of work. Templates answer what to start from; Operating Packs answer how to work within context.

Artifact boundary stays visibleSource and availability stay separateReuse before local creation

What belongs here

Templates own reusable starting structure.

Persona-Library owns Template identity, applicability, relationships, source metadata, evidence, and lifecycle context. The actual reusable artifact may live in rickvang/template-library, a project workspace, or another authorized source.

Known Templates

Search and filter by category, lifecycle status, source kind, and availability. Inspect what a Template provides, when it applies, where the source is expected to live, and which relationships are actually known.

0 Templates

Use the lifecycle honestly

A project starter becomes a canonical Template only after evidence shows that its structure is useful beyond one project and the source, boundary, and relationships are clear.

Discover and evaluate

Search the catalog first. Compare purpose, category, use-when, provided structure, source evidence, status, and task-level applicability. Use $template-research when the fit or reusable boundary is uncertain.

Reuse or create locally

Reuse or adapt a suitable artifact. If none fits, compose the smallest useful local starter and keep project-specific content separate.

Promote when reusable

Catalog a Template only when broader reuse is supported. Reconcile affected Skills, Operating Packs, Playbooks, Tools, Docs, and Site output.

01 / SEARCHFind the starting pointUse the catalog and source evidence before creating a duplicate.
02 / CHECKTest applicabilityConfirm the Persona, Skill, workflow, and ownership relationship when scoped.
03 / ADAPTShape the projectInstantiate or adapt the artifact while keeping output and method separate.
04 / PROMOTEMake reuse visiblePromote only when evidence supports a canonical starting structure.

What a Template does not do

It provides a starting artifact; it does not run the work.

Skills own reusable expertise and judgment. Operating Packs own contextual rules and validation guidance. Tools act under scope and permissions. Playbooks coordinate stages, handoffs, approvals, gates, and outcomes. A Template may be instantiated with a Tool or used under an Operating Pack, but it grants no access and replaces none of those responsibilities.
